system.name: Parcelworks
system.summary: Parcels come in through intake, wait in a durable SQLite queue, and are claimed by a worker under a time-limited lease. The worker routes each one: book a carrier, park it on hold, or fail the attempt and retry with backoff. A report counts what happened.
system.purpose: A parcel is accepted once, gets a carrier label, and is counted as delivered in the report. Refusing, holding and failing for good are deliberate answers, not crashes.

stages.title: Intake
stages.blurb: A parcel request is checked, then refused or put in line.

stages.title: Queue
stages.blurb: Durable jobs in SQLite, claimed under a lease.

stages.title: Work
stages.blurb: The worker loop routes each claimed parcel.

stages.title: Retry and hold
stages.blurb: Backoff retries, terminal failure, and parked parcels.

stages.title: Report
stages.blurb: Counts outcomes and saves the report file.

web.submit.title: Web client sends a parcel
web.submit.plain: The web status client posts the parcel to /api/parcels and gets back an accepted receipt or a refused answer with a reason code. Server errors are retried 3 times, then thrown.
web.submit.why: The only way a person outside the machine reaches intake.
web.submit.failure: A 5xx answer is retried 3 times, then an Error is thrown

intake.submit.title: Take the submit request
intake.submit.plain: The submit command wraps intake. It answers ok with a receipt, or ok false with the refusal code and message. A refusal is an answer, not a crash.

intake.required.title: Check required fields
intake.required.plain: Id, sender, recipient, postcode and weight_g must all be present and non-empty. A zero weight counts as missing.

intake.weight.title: Check weight against limit
intake.weight.plain: The weight must be a positive whole number of grams and at most MAX_WEIGHT_G (30000 by default). Anything else is refused as bad_weight or overweight.
intake.weight.why: Keeps parcels the carrier cannot take out of the queue.

intake.format.title: Check postcode and service
intake.format.plain: The postcode must be 5 capital letters or digits. The service must be standard or express, and defaults to standard.

intake.dedupe.title: Look for a duplicate id
intake.dedupe.plain: accept asks the queue whether this parcel id already exists. A repeat id is refused and nothing is overwritten.

intake.lane.title: Choose the lane
intake.lane.plain: With FAST_LANE on, an express parcel of 500 g or less skips the queue. With it off, which is the default, every parcel takes the normal lane.

intake.fast_done.title: Record as done at intake
intake.fast_done.plain: The parcel is stored already done, with no carrier label and no worker involved. Used only when FAST_LANE=1.
intake.fast_done.why: Lets tiny express parcels skip the backlog.

intake.enqueue.title: Put the parcel in line
intake.enqueue.plain: The parcel is stored as a pending job and a normal-lane receipt is returned.

intake.refused.title: Parcel refused
intake.refused.plain: The caller gets the refusal code and message and nothing is stored. Codes: missing_field, bad_weight, overweight, bad_postcode, bad_service, duplicate.

heard.how: cmd_submit returns ok false with the code and message

queue.pending.title: Jobs waiting in line
queue.pending.plain: Each accepted parcel is a row in the jobs table with status pending. A job can be claimed once its available_at time has passed, which is how backoff delays work.

queue.claim.title: Claim the oldest ready job
queue.claim.plain: One transaction picks the oldest pending job that is ready and returns it, or returns nothing if no job is ready.
queue.claim.why: Only one worker can lease a given job at a time.

queue.leased.title: Job leased to a worker
queue.leased.plain: While leased, the job belongs to one worker until lease_until (LEASE_SECONDS, 30 by default). Claiming also adds one to its attempts. Only the holder of the lease token can complete, fail or hold it.

queue.reclaim.title: Reclaim expired leases
queue.reclaim.plain: Before every claim, jobs whose lease ran out go back in line, or are failed if they already used their last attempt. A crashed worker's job is not lost.
queue.reclaim.why: A worker that dies mid-job must not strand it.
queue.reclaim.failure: Out of attempts: the job is failed with 'lease expired on final attempt'

queue.complete.title: Mark the job done
queue.complete.plain: Marks a leased job done and stores its carrier label. It only works for the current lease token; a worker whose lease expired and was re-claimed gets False and drops its result.
queue.complete.failure: False when the lease token no longer matches

queue.done.title: Finished jobs
queue.done.plain: Done jobs stay in the table. The report counts them as delivered, and the web client's wait stops when it sees one.

work.loop.title: Run the worker loop
work.loop.plain: Ticks until a tick cap is reached or, with stop_when_idle, the queue is empty. Counts how many times each ending happened. A running service sets neither stop.

work.tick.title: Run one job
work.tick.plain: One pass: reclaim expired leases, claim a job, run the handler, then settle the attempt as done, held, retry, failed or lease_lost.

work.idle.title: Sleep while idle
work.idle.plain: When nothing is ready the worker sleeps idle_s seconds and tries again. A job waiting out its backoff looks the same as an empty queue.

work.route.title: Route the parcel
work.route.plain: A declared value over the customs limit without cleared papers is parked, and so is a ZZ postcode. Everything else goes to the carrier.

work.book.title: Book the carrier
work.book.plain: A pretend carrier call returns a label like LBL-pw-1. Outage-zone postcodes (99xxx) always raise TransientError.

work.lease_lost.title: Lease lost, work dropped
work.lease_lost.plain: The worker's lease was gone when it tried to settle, because another claim replaced it. Its result is thrown away so the job is not settled twice.
why2: trace.py@1: no lease expired in this run

trouble.fail.title: Record the failed attempt
trouble.fail.plain: A TransientError counts as a failed attempt. With tries left (MAX_ATTEMPTS, 4 by default) the job returns to pending with a delay. Out of tries, it is failed for good.
trouble.fail.why: Keeps a flaky carrier from losing parcels while still stopping a hopeless one.

trouble.backoff.title: Wait out the backoff
trouble.backoff.plain: The retry cannot be claimed until now plus base times 2 to the (attempt minus 1) seconds: 2, 4, 8 by default, capped at 300.

trouble.failed.title: Terminal failure
trouble.failed.plain: No tries left: the job is failed for good and the report counts it as a dead letter. Reached by the last failed attempt, or by a lease that expired on the last attempt.

heard.how: kept as failed; shows only if someone runs report

trouble.hold_customs.title: Customs hold
trouble.hold_customs.plain: A declared value over CUSTOMS_LIMIT_CENTS (50000 by default) parks the job in hold. Only an operator's release request with paperwork moves it.
trouble.hold_customs.why: Customs paperwork arrives outside the system.
trouble.hold_customs.failure: Waits until a later release request arrives

trouble.hold_address.title: Address hold
trouble.hold_address.plain: A ZZ postcode parks the job in hold as an address hold. The release command answers still on hold for these, and no other code moves a job out of hold.
trouble.hold_address.why: The region cannot be verified automatically.
trouble.hold_address.failure: The web client's wait ends in PollTimeout for a held job

trouble.release.title: Release a customs hold
trouble.release.plain: A later operator request. A customs hold with paperwork given is released and marked cleared so routing lets it through. Without paperwork the answer is still on hold (customs).

trouble.release_refused.title: Answer still on hold
trouble.release_refused.plain: For an address hold the release command only answers still on hold (address) and changes nothing. No release is written for address holds.

report.summarize.title: Count parcels by outcome
report.summarize.plain: Counts done, failed and held jobs under their Outcome names: delivered, dead_letter, held. Jobs still pending or leased are not outcomes yet.

report.render.title: Write the report text
report.render.plain: Lays the counts out as text: one row per outcome name, then lists of held parcels with their reason, dead letters with their last error, and delivered labels.

report.write.title: Save the report file
report.write.plain: Writes a temp file and swaps it into place. If that fails with an OS error it waits and tries again, with no cap on the number of tries.
report.write.failure: OSError sends it to the wait box

report.busy.title: Wait and try again
report.busy.plain: Sleeps min(2 to the attempt, 30) seconds, then loops back to the write. No attempt limit is written in the code.

report.saved.title: Report saved
report.saved.plain: The report path is returned to the caller.

report.returned.title: Returned to sender
report.returned.plain: An outcome name the report prints as a row, always 0. It is declared in Outcome, but no code sets a parcel to it.

r_web_submit.why: The toy has no HTTP server; the request is assumed to reach cmd_submit.

r_submit_required.why: cmd_submit calls accept, which calls validate first.

r_required_ok.why: Every required key is present and non-empty.

r_required_bad.why: The first empty or missing key raises Refusal missing_field.

r_weight_ok.why: A positive whole number of grams at or under MAX_WEIGHT_G.

r_weight_bad.why: Not a positive whole number raises bad_weight; above MAX_WEIGHT_G raises overweight.

r_shape_ok.why: The postcode matches the 5-character pattern and the service is standard or express.

r_shape_bad.why: A malformed postcode raises bad_postcode; an unknown service raises bad_service.

r_dedupe_new.why: The queue has no row with this id.

r_dedupe_dup.why: The queue already has a row with this id, so intake raises Refusal duplicate.

r_lane_fast.why: config.fast_lane() is true, the service is express and the weight is 500 g or less.

r_lane_normal.why: FAST_LANE is off, or the parcel is not express, or it weighs over 500 g.

r_fast_done.why: The job row is written with status done, so it joins the finished jobs the report counts.

r_enqueue_pending.why: enqueue inserts the row with status pending.

r_pending_loop.why: Pending is a table state, not code: the worker reaches the job by claiming it on its next tick.

r_reclaim_ok.why: reclaim_expired found no leased row past its lease_until, so the pass goes on to claim.

r_reclaim_requeue.why: An expired lease with attempts below MAX_ATTEMPTS goes back to pending, available now.

r_reclaim_fail.why: An expired lease on the final attempt is failed for good.

r_claim_leased.why: A pending row with available_at in the past exists; it is leased to this worker.

r_claim_empty.why: No pending row is ready, so claim returns nothing and process_one returns None.

r_leased_route.why: The worker hands the leased job's parcel to the handler.

r_complete_ok.why: The update matched the job, the lease token and status leased, so one row changed.

r_complete_lost.why: No row matched the token because the lease expired and the job was claimed again; the worker drops its result.

r_done_report.why: The report command is a separate request; nothing in the worker triggers it.

r_done_loop.why: After a job settles, run counts the ending and starts the next tick unless max_ticks is reached.

r_loop_tick.why: Each loop turn runs process_one once.

r_tick_reclaim.why: process_one always reclaims expired leases before it claims.

r_idle_loop.why: After the sleep, the loop continues with its next tick.

r_route_customs.why: declared_cents is above CUSTOMS_LIMIT_CENTS and the parcel has no customs_cleared mark.

r_route_address.why: The region cannot be verified, so the parcel is parked as an address hold.

r_route_book.why: No customs or address condition applies.

r_book_ok.why: The carrier call returned a label, so the worker completes the job with it.

r_book_down.why: The carrier call raised TransientError, so the attempt is recorded as failed.

r_fail_retry.why: attempts is below MAX_ATTEMPTS, so the job is set back to pending with a later available_at.

r_fail_final.why: attempts has reached MAX_ATTEMPTS, so the job is set to failed.

r_fail_lost.why: No leased row matches this token, so fail answers stale and the worker reports lease_lost.

r_backoff_pending.why: The row is already pending; it becomes claimable once available_at is in the past.

r_hold_customs_release.why: A later request. No timer or worker code sends it; only an operator calling the release command does.

r_hold_address_release.why: A later request. The command looks the job up, finds an address hold, and answers still on hold.

r_release_ok.why: release_hold marks the parcel customs_cleared, resets attempts and sets the job back to pending.

r_release_no_papers.why: The flag is missing, so the command answers still on hold (customs) and changes nothing.

r_release_other.why: Nothing changed: the job stays in hold until another request arrives, and the next one gets the same answer.

r_sum_render.why: publish passes the summary straight to render.

r_render_write.why: publish passes the text straight to write_report.

r_write_saved.why: The temp file replaced the report path, so the path is returned.

r_write_busy.why: Any OSError while writing or swapping the file is caught and counted as an attempt.

r_busy_write.why: The while True loop starts the write again; nothing in the code ends it except a success.

paths.title: Main path
paths.blurb: One ordinary parcel from request to saved report.

paths.title: Carrier outage to terminal failure
paths.blurb: An outage-zone parcel goes round the retry loop, waiting longer each lap, until MAX_ATTEMPTS and then fails for good.

paths.title: Customs hold and release
paths.blurb: A high-value parcel is parked until an operator sends a release with paperwork.

paths.title: Address hold
paths.blurb: A ZZ postcode is parked. A release request gets the answer still on hold, every time.

paths.title: Fast lane
paths.blurb: With FAST_LANE on, a small express parcel is stored as done at intake.

loops.title: Retry with backoff
loops.blurb: A failed carrier call sends the job back to pending with a growing delay.
loops.limit: MAX_ATTEMPTS tries per job (4 by default), then terminal failure

loops.title: Worker loop
loops.blurb: Tick, claim, route, settle, tick again.
loops.limit: max_ticks or stop_when_idle; a running service sets neither

loops.title: Report write retry
loops.blurb: A busy destination makes the writer sleep and try the whole write again.

loops.title: Customs hold and release
loops.blurb: A release request either frees the job or leaves it on hold.
loops.limit: Each lap needs a new operator request

loops.title: Address hold and answer
loops.blurb: A release request is answered and the job stays on hold.
loops.limit: Each lap needs a new operator request

heardWords.caller: thrown or returned to the code that called
heardWords.unclear: the code does not settle it

findings.question: Outcome lists "returned_to_sender" but no ending in the code sets it: is it kept for later, or left over?
findings.evidence: Outcome declares "returned_to_sender" (parcelworks/schema.py:14), and the census finds no ending that produces it. No code refers to Outcome.RETURNED. Assignments and dict literals were not searched (no signals.json with a produced list: run faultline signals), so a value set only that way would not be seen. The box has no road in. Another check finds the same boxes (no way in): No road comes in; 0 roads go out. The box's kind is end.

resolution.why: Outcome.RETURNED is declared and printed in every report as zero, but no code path assigns it; kept as a suspect for the owner to decide

findings.question: 1 road in, every road on leads back to the same 2 boxes: what lets flow out of trouble.hold_address reach an ending?
findings.evidence: 2 boxes reach no ending by any road. 1 road comes in, from work.route. Inside, the roads run from trouble.hold_address to trouble.release_refused, when "Operator sends release"; from trouble.release_refused to trouble.hold_address. The way on waits for an outside event ("Operator sends release").

resolution.why: a ZZ postcode is parked and the release command answers 'still on hold' every time; confirmed by the address-hold walk

findings.question: No test or run reached the outcome "stale" at parcelworks/worker.py:28: what would make it happen, and is it worth a test?
findings.evidence: Not seen in the loaded test evidence: outcome "stale" at parcelworks/worker.py:28; outcome "lease_lost" at parcelworks/worker.py:32 (trace.py@1: no lease expired in this run).

resolution.why: no test and no run reaches the lease-lost ending; coverage shows worker.py line 32 never ran

findings.question: Loop "Report write retry" shows no limit: what stops it?
findings.evidence: No limit is shown on the loop. Code shows a retry at parcelworks/report.py:38 (while True; exits only on success (line 43), no count or limit).

resolution.why: write_report retries on OSError with while True and no count; only a success ends it
